cards.text: It's Pentecost in Jerusalem. The Holy Spirit just came on Jesus' followers, they're speaking in other tongues, and some in the crowd are saying they're drunk on new wine (Acts 2:1-13). Then Peter, one of Jesus' apostles, stands up with the other eleven, lifts up his voice and tells the whole crowd to listen carefully.

cards.question: Peter gives the crowd his reason these men aren't drunk: it's already late at night.

cards.text: It's only the third hour of the day, the hour when most folks are still ARGUING with the snooze button. No, Peter says, this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel (Joel 2:28-32).

cards.question: In the words Peter quotes from Joel, who does God say He will pour out His Spirit on in the last days?

cards.text: It's ALL people: sons and daughters will prophesy, young men will see visions, old men will dream dreams, and God will pour out His Spirit even on menservants and maidservants. Friend, nobody's getting turned away at the door over a job title.

Then Joel's words turn to the sky: God will show wonders in the heavens, signs on the earth, blood and fire and billows of smoke. The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood, before the great and glorious Day of the Lord.

cards.question: After all those signs, Joel's words end with a promise that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.

cards.text: Now Peter turns to the Man at the center of it all: Jesus of Nazareth, certified by God with miracles, wonders and signs right among these people. And Peter basically says, don't act brand new, you KNOW this.

cards.question: Peter says Jesus was delivered up by a set plan and foreknowledge. Whose?

cards.text: And Peter doesn't tiptoe. He tells this crowd that they, by the hands of the lawless, put Jesus to death by nailing Him to the cross.

cards.question: Peter says God raised Jesus from the dead, because it was impossible for death to keep Him in its grip.

cards.text: Then Peter pulls out the heavyweight: David, Israel's king, and quotes Psalm 16. David says, “I saw the Lord always before me; because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.”

cards.question: David says God won't abandon his soul to Hades, nor let His Holy One see decay. Because of this, how does David say his heart is?

cards.text: David's words end with the paths of life and joy in God's presence. Then Peter tells them with confidence: David died, he was buried, and his tomb is still right there with them to this day.

cards.question: Peter says David was a prophet, and God had promised him on oath to put one of his descendants on his throne. So who was David really talking about?

answers.text: The Christ rising from the dead
His son Solomon on the throne

cards.question: Peter tells the crowd he's the only one who can vouch that God raised Jesus to life.
Peter says ___ has been exalted to the right hand of God, has received the promised Holy Spirit from the Father, and has poured out what the crowd now sees and hears.

cards.text: David did not ascend into heaven, Peter says. But David himself says, in Psalm 110:1, “The Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.’”

cards.question: Peter's big finish: let all Israel know with certainty that God has made this Jesus, whom they crucified, both Lord and ___.

cards.text: When the people hear all this, they're cut to the heart. Not a little uncomfortable. CUT. TO. THE. HEART.

cards.question: Cut to the heart, what does the crowd ask Peter and the other apostles?

answers.text: Brothers why did no one warn us

cards.question: Peter answers the crowd with two things for every one of them to do. What are they?
Peter tells the crowd to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of their ___.

cards.text: Peter says they'll receive the gift of the Holy Spirit, the same Spirit who was just poured out right in front of them. And to think some of these folks showed up sure somebody was tipsy at the third hour of the day.

cards.question: Peter says the promise he's just made belongs only to the people standing in front of him that day.

cards.text: It's for them, their children, and all who are far off, all whom the Lord our God will call to Himself. With many other words Peter keeps testifying, and he urges them, “Be saved from this corrupt generation.”

cards.question: Only a handful of people embrace Peter's message and are baptized that day.

cards.text: Those who embraced his message were baptized, and about THREE THOUSAND were added to the believers that day. Friend, my first welcome in the junk drawer was ONE scared can opener, and I thought THAT was a big day.
The new believers devote themselves to the apostles' teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.

cards.question: A sense of awe comes over everyone, and the ___ perform many wonders and signs.

cards.text: All the believers are together and have everything in common.

cards.question: The believers sell their possessions and goods and share with anyone who is in need.

cards.text: With one accord they keep meeting daily in the temple courts, and they break bread from house to house, with gladness and sincerity of heart. Thousands of people with one accord, when most group chats of SIX can fall apart over one emoji.

cards.question: The believers are praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And what does the Lord do, day after day?

answers.text: Adds to their number those being saved
Opens prison doors for the apostles
Sends them out to other nations
